subject: Marketing Strategy
text: Tesla, Inc. is evaluating opportunities to expand its electric vehicle presence in new international markets. The company is considering increasing its operations in India Brazil, and Germany. Senior management wants to systematically evaluate these markets before committing major investments. Initial market research has revealed the following insights: The growth rate of the EV market, government incentives, availability of charging infrastructure, and consumer environmental awareness differ significantly across these three countries. Tesla’s brand awareness, distribution and service network, pricing competitiveness, and technological advantage vary in each market. Future trends such as government policies on emissions, fuel prices, competition from local EV manufacturers, and technological developments in batteries are expected to influence the long-term attractiveness of these markets. To make an informed strategic decision, Tesla’s management team decides to use a Market Attractiveness/Competitive Position Matrix. Recommend how Tesla could construct in 5 steps, a Market Attractiveness/Competitive Position Matrix to evaluate the three potential markets.

subject: Marketing Strategy
question_stem: Starbucks is one of the world’s leading coffeehouse brands and is known for delivering
text: strong customer experience and high perceived value. The company focuses on understanding customer preferences for premium coffee, comfortable store environments, and personalized service. Starbucks invests heavily in quality sourcing of coffee beans, product innovation, and store design to ensure consistent product quality. It also uses strong marketing communication, loyalty programs, and digital engagement through the Starbucks app to build customer relationships. Although Starbucks products are often priced higher than competitors, customers perceive the brand as offering superior quality, atmosphere, and service, which enhances the overall value they receive. This strategy has helped Starbucks achieve strong customer loyalty global growth, and high profitability. With reference to the Starbucks case, explain how the company applies the process of Customer Value Management (minimum 5 criteria) to deliver superior value to its customers.

subject: Marketing Strategy
text: Dyson is known for introducing innovative household technologies such as the Dyson Supersonic and advanced bagless vacuum cleaners. When Dyson introduced the Supersonic hair dryer, the company priced the product significantly higher than traditional hair dryers available in the market. Dyson targeted professional hairstylists and premium consumers who value advanced technology, superior performance, and unique design. The product was launched with limited distribution initially, strong technological differentiation, and a high price, emphasizing its advanced motor technology, faster drying time, and protection from heat damage. Because of its innovative features and premium positioning, early adopters were willing to pay a higher price for the product despite the presence of cheaper alternatives in the market. Infer the strategy used by Dyson, a new product pioneer, with reference to this case. State two situation variables that characterise this strategy.

subject: Marketing Strategy
text: Unilever operates in more than 190 countries and manages a large portfolio of brands such as Dove, Axe, and Surf Excel. For many years, the company organized its marketing and sales activities primarily by geographic regions. However, with rapid changes in global markets, increasing digitalization, and evolving customer preferences, Unilever began facing several challenges. Consumers across different countries started demanding more personalized products, faster innovation, and consistent global brand experiences. At the same time, marketing and sales teams required better access to customer data, market insights, and coordination across regions. The company also realized that some regional structures created duplication of work, slower decision-making, and higher operational costs. Additionally, new digital marketing capabilities and global supply chain resources were becoming increasingly important for maintaining competitiveness. As a result, senior management at Unilever started considering whether the company should restructure its marketing and sales organization to better respond to these changing market conditions. Based on the case, analyze how managers should strategize (5 points) whether it is the right time to restructure the organization.

text: Coca-Cola has successfully maintained its market leadership by closely observing shifts in consumer behavior and adjusting its strategies accordingly. The company introduced options like Coca-Cola Zero, Diet Coke, and bottled water to cater to the evolving preferences of health-conscious consumers. By staying attuned to consumer needs and market trends, Coca-Cola effectively navigated changes in the beverage industry. text: Urban Company has introduced ‘Insta Maids,’ a new maid-for-hire service that provides users with domestic help within 15 minutes. With this launch the home services startup is venturing into the quick commerce sector. Currently in the pilot phase, ‘Insta Maids’ is being tested in Mumbai, with potential expansion to other cities where Urban Company operates, as reported by Moneycontrol. According to a Facebook post by the company, the service starts at Rs 245 per hour, but as an introductory offer, users can access it for Rs 49 an hour. “The new service is available for Rs 49 per hour. ‘Your maid took an off but your chores won’t! Get a UC Insta Maid in just 15 mins to tackle it all. Starts @ only Rs 49/hour!’” the company said in a recent Facebook post. The service covers tasks such as utensil cleaning, brooming mopping, and cooking preparation, among other household chores. The company has now entered the quick commerce market, joining major players in the rapid delivery space. Urban Company’s existing services include bathroom, kitchen, and full-home cleaning, sofa and carpet cleaning, and pest control solutions for termites, bed bugs, cockroaches, ants, and general pests. Appraise the potential sources of competitive advantage for Pioneer Strategy (minimum 5 points)

text: UNIQLO unveils its latest Spring Summer campaign, ‘Life in Linen’, starring Bollywood actors and UNIQLO brand endorsers, Kareena and Sidharth Ahead of peak summer season, this campaign highlights the elegance and versatility of UNIQLO's Premium Linen Collection.The campaign positions linen as a comfortable and stylish choice for summer through two films showing the actors in everyday settings. text: Case Study Read the case and answer the questions given at the end. FAST FOOD TURNS HEALTHY There are many reasons why consumers around the world have made the fast food industry one of the fastest growing over the last four decades, but healthy eating isn’t one of them. At least not until Subway, the ubiquitous American Sandwich Chain decided in the late 1990's that its downscale image had to go. Subway has grown from a single store in 1965 to a nationwide chain of stores whose sales volume had long since surpassed $1 billion. But it was known more for its belly-busting foot long sandwiches and its gaudy yellow decor than for anything else. Subway needed a makeover- a new position in the marketplace that would distinguish subway from its fat- and sugar-purveying competitors. The Jared Diet Fortuitously for Subway, at about the same time as the company decided to remake its image by adding healthier sandwiches, a rotund college student at Indiana University who happened to live next door to the local subway outlet decided that getting winded by dragging his 425- pound body across the campus wasn’t much fun. Jared Fogle, a regular customer of the subway store saw the healthier sandwiches — less than 7 grams of fat, the signs proclaimed- and decided it was time to go on a diet. For lunch it would be a six-inch turkey, no mayo, no oil and hold the cheese please. For dinner a footlong veggie sub, a bag of baked potato chips and a diet beverage. The other element in his weight loss strategy was walking. No more riding the bus. No more elevators. “Walking was the key” said Fogle.   walked an average of 1.5 miles a day, five days a week. It may not sound a lot but it was sure better than what   was doing. A year later he was down to 180 pounds in his 6 foot- 2 inch frame. An editor at the student newspaper wrote about Jared’s feat, the national media picked up the story and before long Fogle was Subway’s spokesman — Jared, the Subway Guy. a! Repositioning Fuels Subway’s Growth To reflect the new positioning stores interiors were updated. The dated graphics depicting New York City were dumped, and pictures of fresh tomatoes and other vegetables took their place. New Hearty- healthy Sandwiches and later, Atkins friendly wraps — bowing to the growing “fe popularity of the carbohydrate controlled Atkins diet were introduced. And Jared went on a national tour, appearing in more than two dozen heart walks a year, as well as talk shows everywhere. Subways new image as a place where you could get healthy fast food and all the hoopla Jared generated paid the chains and its franchisees a twofold dividend. It helped stores grow their sales as concerns over obesity became a compelling health issue at the dawn of a new millennium. And it enticed more people to sign up as franchisees and open new Subway stores in the United States and abroad. The results? In 2001, Subway surpassed McDonalds as the most ubiquitous fast food operator in the United States, with 13,247 stores at year-end, opening 904 stores to McDonalds 295. Now the world’s largest submarine sandwich chain, Subway by mid-2006 had more than 25000 stores in 84 countries. Q a. Critically analyze the marketing environment of Subway and explain how they have converted their threats into opportunities and covered their weakness with their own strength. Q b.
